messages.content: How do algorithms on content platforms generally decide what to show more people?

Most platforms use some version of early engagement signals to decide whether to push content wider. When you post, it typically goes out to a small initial pool first — maybe your existing followers or a small test group. The platform watches specific signals in that first window: how many people watch to completion, comment, share, or save it, and how quickly those actions happen after posting.

If that early engagement rate beats a threshold relative to similar content, the algorithm expands distribution to a bigger pool and repeats the test. If it underperforms, distribution usually just stops there quietly rather than being actively 'punished.'

Honestly, this is why posting consistency and strong hooks in the first few seconds matter so much — you're not just making content, you're passing (or failing) a series of small tests almost immediately after posting.
